The red and blue shapes and the short lines are piled into that same strip, a long diagonal line cuts across the left side, and the green shape floats just above the headline, so the original's icon-over-headline arrangement is gone. Its green and blue corner triangles have been turned into odd floating shapes in the middle of the right half, and the line accents are scattered at random, so the right side looks arbitrary and the balance is lopsided.

A rearranges the layout: the turbine and the three-line headline are larger and dominant, but the cluster sits left of centre (about x=320 on a 768 canvas). The decorative green, blue and red shapes now float inside the canvas with flat, cropped edges instead of running off the edges as in the original, so they look like clipped fragments. B is just a shrunken copy of the original pillarboxed in the middle: all the decorations stop at a hard invisible edge near x=125 and x=640, leaving dead side margins. Its headline and turbine are noticeably smaller, so B fails fit-to-format.

A and B are nearly pixel-identical. Both keep the purple headline panel centred and readable. Both have the same flaws: a faint, lighter translucent band runs edge to edge behind the panel and looks like a leftover artifact, and the photo is crop-zoomed and visibly soft. The panel also crowds the left edge more than the right. A's headline is a hair larger with slightly tighter leading, and B's has marginally more padding. That difference isn't enough to separate them.

Both are the original squeezed into a leaderboard rather than redesigned for it. The three-line headline stays stacked in a small centred purple box, when this banner shape calls for a single horizontal line. The type is tiny at this size and leaves big areas of busy, blurry photo on either side, and the crop loses the furniture scene that gave the original its meaning. In A, the purple box runs nearly edge to edge vertically, so the text feels jammed against the top and bottom. B leaves a little more breathing room around the box, so it is marginally better, but the two are essentially the same failed resize.

The two are almost identical: each crops tightly into the shelf, curtain and sofa area, so the original's vase, yellow side table and glassware are lost, and the zoomed photo looks soft. Each puts the purple headline box at the vertical centre with a busy shelf above and an empty blurred sofa below. A wins only slightly because its box has more even side margins (about 26px) and roomier padding around the headline; B's box sits closer to the canvas edges (about 18px) and its slightly bigger headline crowds the box, so the box no longer feels as well proportioned to the canvas.

A keeps the chef-hat, tools, dome and plate emblem together as one centred unit, scaled up to suit the square canvas. Its only flaws are that the 'B' and 'Y' of 'BBQ PARTY' run past the dome's edges onto the busy meat photo (as in the original), and the cleaver blade crowds the dome. B breaks the emblem apart: a huge chef hat sits on its own top-left over the meat, the cleaver and spatula are scattered tiny on the white noodles, red line pieces float loose mid-canvas, and the shrunken headline dome is pushed off to the right. That kills the hierarchy and the original logo-like look.

A turns the layout into a clean centred vertical stack (date, divider, headline, subhead, GROVE.ONLINE ribbon) with the illustration cluster below it, so the reading order matches the original. Its flaws are minor: the thimble and pins sit close to the left edge, and the space between the ribbon and the art is a little tight. B shrinks 'JULY 29' into a tiny two-line label crammed beside the headline, leaves the divider stranded in a large dead gap, and pushes 'FOR BEGINNERS' to the bottom edge, away from the headline it qualifies. That breaks both the hierarchy and the grouping.

A reads cleanly left to right. The headline is clearly dominant, and the subhead sits centred above it. Its flaws: the photo is a tiny thumbnail beside a dead empty left margin, and the decorative squares are scattered, with the bottom pair jammed right against the 'P' of PLAYFUL. B butts the photo against the left edge and crops it, and enlarges the squares into a heavy, meaningless blocky glyph. It also leaves a large dead gap in the middle and squeezes the two-line PLAYFUL/LEARNING headline against the right canvas edge with no margin, beside the subhead, which looks cramped and lopsided.

A is close to a scaled copy of the original. The skates are cropped hard at the top, the ICE RINK headline is small for a 614-wide canvas, the margins are wide and empty, and the decorative rings at the left and right edges are clipped awkwardly. Still, the offer block, the divider and the CTA stay aligned and readable. B has a decorative ring sitting on top of the skate illustration in several places, and the arrow's tail collides with the skate blade. Its offer block is broken: USE CODE and XMASRINK no longer line up, 50% OFF is shrunk to fine print below TO GET A DISCOUNT, and the CTA is jammed against the code text.

A: dark decorative rings sit directly on the white skate boots, which looks like a collision. The code block is cramped: 'USE CODE' and 'XMASRINK' crowd the divider lines, and the right column's baseline doesn't line up with the left. The skates are cropped hard at the top so the laces are lost, and the arrow tail touches the blade. B: the code block has clean, even spacing, with the CTA and headline properly ranked. Its flaws: the skates are still cropped at the top, two rings clip the skate's toe and blade, the arrow starts on the blade, and ICE crowds the skate's heel.

A: the 'Happy Easter' lettering is blown up so far that 'Easter' sits right across the bunny, the basket and the sweater, and 'FUN GROUP' sits on top of the bicycle wheels. The bike is also cut off at the bottom edge and the leaf garlands are gone, though 'Happy' is still readable on white and still reads as the headline. B: the shrunken gold headline sits completely on the busy bunny and basket, so it is hard to read, and it collides with the bunny's face. 'FUN GROUP' has moved above the headline, which flips the reading order and lets the small brand line compete as the main focal point. The bike is cropped at the bottom here too, leaving dead white space at the top and a crowded lower half.

A is the original dropped unchanged into the centre of the wider canvas. The brush strokes no longer bleed off the edges, which leaves empty white bands on both sides, and the headline now covers only about half the width, so it reads small and weak. B scales the headline back up to the original's width and keeps the photo collage. However, the photos shrank and the left one is cropped narrower. The headline is also jammed right under the pink stroke's black dots, and the chevron and 'Swipe up' are packed tight beneath it, so the bottom feels cramped while the side margins stay empty.

A keeps the original collage, the brush strokes and the text stack, but it is basically a shrunk copy. The headline wraps into five cramped lines with the word '10' stranded on its own line, there is large dead space above and below, and the pink stroke crowds the photo edge. B has fallen apart: the first photo is a tiny sliver, the brush strokes and the swipe chevron are lined up in an arbitrary row, and the second photo floats alone. 'Swipe up' is pushed to the left away from its chevron, and the brand collage feel is lost.

A keeps related items together: the brand block (logo, Huzzah, Since 1982) and the quote with its attribution. But all the info text is microscopic, 'Helen Keller' is squeezed into a cramped two-line wrap against the quote, the woman image is gone, and there is dead space at the left edge. B scatters the pieces: 'Huzzah' crowds against the oversized logo, 'Since 1982' sits orphaned in the far-right corner away from the brand, and 'Helen Keller' floats far from its quote. B also loses the hero image and its text is just as tiny.

Both drop the woman-in-wind photo, which was the key image, and leave only a washed-out sky. In both, the -Helen Keller attribution is pushed to a cramped two-line scrap off to the side of the quote. A: the logo is oversized and the Huzzah/Since 1982 labels butt against its right edge, but the tagline and address form a tidy column and the quote reads clearly. B: the tiny logo collides with Huzzah beneath it, and Since 1982, the tagline and the address are scattered along a bottom row jammed near the edge. Its attribution is also crushed against the right edge, so it reads as fragments rather than a composed banner.

A keeps the ram skull as a strong full-width hero with the yellow bar across it, but the quote is forced into a long column with odd line breaks: 'to' sits alone on its own line and 'men.' and 'the weak.' wrap awkwardly. The attribution is indented off the text's left edge and crammed against the bottom of the canvas. B has the same broken wrapping and the same orphaned 'to'. It also shrinks the ram into a small top-left thumbnail with the yellow bar cut short, so the hero image becomes trivial and the top-right corner is left empty.

A drops the URL and keeps a stray '|' separator after NOVAK GALLERY. Its date wraps awkwardly ('JUNE 5 TO / JULY 3'), an empty white frame box floats on its own detached from the art, and the dot artwork is cropped against the right edge, so the layout looks broken. B keeps all the original info in a neat left-aligned three-line stack and shows the framed dot artwork intact on the right, but the info lines are cramped and tiny at banner size, and the middle text block is crowded against the art while uneven gaps are left elsewhere.

A has a sensible banner layout: a large red headline and info stack on the left and the art on the right, with good hierarchy. Its flaws: the white frame sits off-centre inside the image instead of breaking its edge as in the original, the two black rules float with a big gap above the headline, and there is a stray tick mark above 'ART'. B is worse: the black rules and a tick mark cut across the dot artwork, the white frame is gone, and the headline and info are small and pushed into a cramped column on the right. B also leaves stray vertical line fragments at the bottom and empty white space on the right.

I'd ship neither as is, but B is clearly the better resize. A breaks the headline into four short stacked lines that crowd the left side. The chevrons are blown up to a huge size in the bottom-left, where they compete with the nurse illustration. The nurse is pushed to the right, and her flat-cut lower edge now floats above the canvas bottom when it should run off the edge, so the composition looks lopsided and arbitrary. B keeps the original's centred order (headline, then chevrons, then nurse) with sensible two-line wrapping and the right hierarchy. However, its illustration also stops short of the bottom edge, leaving a visible band of empty background below the crop line that looks like a mistake, and the space between headline, chevrons and figure feels slightly tight.

A: the headline wraps to five lines and leaves 'us' as an orphan, running almost to the side edges. The nurse illustration no longer bleeds off the bottom: its cropped edge floats above an empty blue band, though the chevron stays in proportion and the hierarchy holds. B: the headline wraps better ('chose us' stays together), but the chevron is blown up until it competes with the headline. That leaves a dead gap above it and shrinks the nurse to a small floating cutout with the same visible crop and empty band at the bottom.

Both versions have the same structural problems. The two white bars are pushed out to the extreme top and bottom edges, far from the headline panel, so the original's framing (bars overlapping the dark box) is lost. The headline is far too small for a tall story format, leaving huge empty stretches of blurry, upscaled background above and below. A is worse: its panel is narrower and its headline smaller, so it reads as a shrunk copy. B's wider panel and slightly larger type give the headline a bit more presence, but it is still undersized and floats in dead space.

A: the decorative arrows are blown up, blurry and crammed to the left of 'YOUR EFFICIENT' instead of flanking it. The key illustration is shrunk to a small postage stamp in the lower left, a stray blue strip hangs off the left edge, and the bottom right is dead empty, so the imagery becomes trivial. B: the centred kicker, headline and full-width illustration keep the original's feel and hierarchy. Its flaws are tiny, faint arrows pushed far from the kicker, awkward mismatched blue background panels behind the art, and the illustration cut off at the bottom edge with the headline close above it.

A has a sensible top-to-bottom order (eyebrow, headline, illustration), but the eyebrow arrows float far from 'YOUR EFFICIENT'. The top ~140px is dead space, the illustration has lost its light-blue backdrop, and two arbitrary light-blue blocks are stuck along the bottom edge. B has a blown-up, blurry left arrow that is badly distorted next to a tiny right one, and a pointless blue strip down the left edge that stops at an arbitrary height. A big gap cuts the eyebrow off from 'ENERGY USE', the headline sits low with empty space below it, and the illustration takes the lead while the headline drops to second place.

Both lose the key image: the woman holding the résumé is gone, apart from a stray fingertip clipped at the bottom-right edge, and a large empty teal field is left behind. A mixes alignments: the headline and 'since 1980' are left-aligned, but the rules, tilde and diamond dots are centred, so the dots float apart from their text. B keeps one left edge for the text and tilde, but a diamond dot collides with the 's' of 'since', the top rules are jammed near the top edge, and the vertical gaps are uneven, with a big dead band above 'since 1980'.

Both resizes drop the woman holding the résumé, which is the original's key image. All that's left is a cropped hand stuck in the bottom-right corner, so neither keeps the design's meaning. A at least keeps the text and rule lines on one left edge, but the left diamond overlaps the 's' of 'since 1980', the right diamond floats loose, and there's a large dead gap above the footer. B is worse: the text is left-aligned while the rules sit on a different centred axis, the flourish drifts off to the right, the diamonds float above and away from 'since 1980', and the footer sits on a third arbitrary indent.

In A, the white headline 'SPARKLING NIGHT', the date and the 'premiere' text are cut off at the image edge and disappear into the white background, and 'DRESSCODE' is clipped to 'ODE: BLACK DRESS'. A is unusable. B is intact and legible, but the 'premiere' line is gone and the headline is small and pushed to the bottom of a narrow photo strip, so the grey dress-code line reads louder than it. B also leaves large empty white areas above and below its right-hand text column.

A splits the key illustration apart: the heart floats on its own and the hand sits cropped and detached beside the second headline, so the main image no longer reads. Its URL also floats at the top on its own, and the secondary headline leaves an orphaned 'THE' on its own line. B keeps the heart and hand together, but they are tiny and jammed against the second headline. B has the same orphaned 'THE', its contact text is crammed into narrow lines that run to the bottom edge, and its URL floats in the middle with nothing beside it. Both are shrunk copies of the original placed side by side with no clear hierarchy, but B at least keeps the main image intact.

A has a clear left-to-right flow: headline and URL, then the heart-and-hand image, then the CTA. But the image is too small, its hand runs into the CTA/contact text block, the follow-us line sits right on the bottom edge, and a large empty gap sits in the middle. B breaks the key image: the heart and hand are pulled apart, leaving the hand as a meaningless grey blob that collides with the CTA. B also squeezes the CTA and contact copy into narrow, ragged columns with bad wrapping and leaves the URL floating on its own.

A: the 'Lima & Co Group' wordmark was moved off its solid navy circle and now sits on the white and gold halftone pattern. The white text on the white disc is almost invisible and 'Group' is lost in the pattern, while the navy circle on the right is left empty. B has the same failure but worse: the brand text is shrunk to a tiny white smudge on the white/gold disc, so it is completely unreadable and the navy area is again empty dead space. A is marginally less bad only because its larger text is partly visible.

Both use the same stacked skyscraper layout. Their shared flaws: the headline sits only about 12px from the left edge, and 'NOT' is orphaned on its own line. In A, the figure ends well above the bottom and floats over a dead green strip, while in the original she stands on the bottom edge. A's starburst does stay neatly left-aligned with the headline. In B, the figure reaches the bottom edge as in the original, so the canvas looks fuller. However, B's starburst is pushed almost against the top edge and is centred rather than aligned to the headline's left edge, so the two don't share a common edge.

A: the TRY NOW starburst floats at an arbitrary spot in the top centre, lining up with neither the headline's left edge nor the figure. The selfie figure is shrunk too small, and a dead band of empty green is left under the headline. B: keeps the original's top-left starburst-over-headline grouping, aligned on the left edge, and the figure is larger and fills the height better. However, the starburst is crammed against the top-left corner, the left margin is tight, and there is still empty space at the bottom.

A splits the design into three columns. The date and address float alone at far right, away from the headline, so related info is broken apart. The headline is small for the canvas, and the striped image sits in the middle with large dead gaps on both sides, which reads as arbitrary. B keeps the original grouping: a large, dominant headline with the date and address stacked under it on a shared left edge, and the image on the right. However, B's whole layout is a centered island with about 140px of empty margin on each side. The image strips also no longer bleed off the edge as they do in the original, which weakens the feel.

A keeps the turbine and headline as a proper lockup, but it is jammed against the left side, touching the top and bottom edges. The green and blue triangles float mid-canvas as random fragments instead of anchoring the corners, so the right two-thirds feel arbitrary and the layout is lopsided. B shrinks the turbine, the key image, to a tiny icon jammed into a cluttered bottom strip with the red and blue shapes and line fragments. A long diagonal line slices across the left, and the green shape sits awkwardly above the headline, so the imagery becomes trivial and the composition looks broken.

A is just the original shrunk into the middle of the wide canvas. The decorative triangles and lines stop at an invisible inner frame (the green and blue shapes end around x≈640, the red starts around x≈125), which leaves dead white bands on both sides, and the windmill and headline are small and lost. B actually rearranges the design: a bigger windmill, a heavier headline that fills the height, and the decorations spread to the sides. But its green and blue shapes now end in hard vertical cuts short of the canvas edge instead of bleeding off it. The line pairs also float without reaching the edges. The headline breaks into three stacked lines with a cramped bottom margin, and the hero sits a little left of centre.

A and B are almost pixel-identical. Both crop the photo hard and upscale it until it is soft and blurry, and both lose the original's vase and much of the room. Both also show a pale, full-width band (roughly y≈170–600) behind the purple panel, which looks like a compositing artifact rather than a deliberate layer. The headline is readable and keeps its hierarchy and brand purple in both; B's text is marginally heavier, but the difference is not meaningful.

Both are essentially the same lazy result. Each keeps the headline stacked on three lines inside a small purple box in the middle of a 728x90 leaderboard, so the original was shrunk rather than rearranged into a single left-to-right line. That leaves the headline only about 15px tall, takes up roughly 20% of the banner's width, and wastes the rest on a cropped, blurry photo strip. A's box has slightly more padding; B's text is a touch larger, but its box nearly touches the top and bottom edges. The differences are too small to matter.

The two candidates are almost identical. Both use the same tight, zoomed crop, which cuts out the original's key furniture: the dark vase and the yellow-black side table with glassware. The image is reduced to blurry shelves and sofa fabric, and the purple headline panel sits a little above centre with the lower half left as busy, empty filler. A's panel and headline run almost edge to edge with only about 18px of side margin, which feels cramped. B's slightly narrower panel leaves about 26px of margin and reads a little more deliberate, but the difference is marginal.

A breaks the logo lockup apart: the chef hat is blown up to a huge white blob floating top-left, the cleaver and spatula are scattered small over the busy radish garnish, and the cloche and 'BBQ PARTY' are shrunk off to the right with a stray red line fragment, so the brand mark and hierarchy are destroyed. B keeps the hat/tools/cloche lockup whole, centred and well scaled so the headline dominates, as in the original. Its only flaws are minor: 'BBQ PARTY' still runs slightly past the dome edges and the photo crop is a bit tighter.

A: 'JULY 29' is shrunk to a tiny two-line label jammed against the left of the headline, so it loses the prominence it had in the original. The red divider is stranded on the left with dead space all around it, there's a big empty band between the headline and the art, and 'FOR BEGINNERS' and the badge are pushed down to the bottom edge. B: keeps the original's centred text stack (date, divider, headline, subline, badge) in the right order and size steps, with the illustration intact below. Minor flaws: the text block is a bit cramped compared with the empty strip at the bottom, and the thimble and pins sit close to the left edge.

A: the photo is a tiny thumbnail pushed to the left edge. The decorative squares are blown up into a heavy, meaningless block in the middle that draws more attention than the title. 'PLAYFUL LEARNING' is jammed against the right edge, and the space between the photo and the text is dead. B: the headline sits on one line with the eyebrow centred above it, which reads well, but the brand squares collide with the photo and butt right up against the 'P' of the headline. The small photo floats off-centre, leaving the left third of the banner empty.

A has clear unwanted collisions: decorative rings sit on top of the skates and the arrow cuts through the blade. The discount block is also broken: 'USE CODE'/'XMASRINK' and 'TO GET A DISCOUNT'/'50% OFF' are on mismatched baselines with uneven spacing, and the headline crowds the right edge. B keeps the original structure cleanly with no collisions, but it reads like a narrow column dropped into a wider canvas. The headline, code block and CTA sit in a slim centre strip with dead space on both sides, and the headline is undersized for the format.

A: the skates are cropped hard at the top edge, losing the hanging laces from the original. Decorative rings collide with the skate toe and blade, and 'ICE' almost touches the blade tip. Even so, the code block is evenly spaced around its divider and the CTA sits centered below it, so the hierarchy holds. B: several rings land on top of the white boots, an obvious unwanted collision. The code block is cramped, with the divider jammed against 'USE CODE' and 'TO GET A DISCOUNT'. The headline, code block and CTA don't share one axis, and the left half of the canvas is mostly empty.

A: the 'Happy Easter' script is small and sits right on the bunny's face and basket, so it is hard to read. 'FUN GROUP' sits above the headline in a size that competes with it, which flips the hierarchy, the leaf garlands are gone and the bike is cut off at the bottom edge. B: the huge headline covers almost the whole bunny, wiping out the key illustration. 'FUN GROUP' sits on the busy bike wheels and is barely readable, and the bike is also cropped, so it is worse on both collisions and legibility.

A shrinks the photo cluster and changes the layering: the pancake photo now sits on top of the croissant photo, and the croissant crop is squashed short. The pink squiggle's dot trail runs right into the oversized headline, and wide empty bands are left on both sides. B keeps the original stacking, crops, scale and spacing between the dots and headline almost exactly. However, it is just the story layout centred on a wider canvas with blank side margins and no real rearrangement, and the pink stroke and dots sit loosely against the right edge.

A breaks up the design. The croissant photo becomes a tiny thumbnail lined up in a row with scattered pink brush strokes, dots and an oversized swipe-up chevron. The pancake photo floats alone, the 'Swipe up' text sits far from its chevron, and the layered collage is lost. B keeps the original layered collage and its order, but squeezes it into a small cluster. The photos are too small to read clearly, the headline wraps awkwardly over 5 lines with '10' left alone on the first line, and there's empty space at the top and a big dead area under 'Swipe up'.

In A, 'Since 1982' has been split from the logo and left as an orphan at the far-right edge. The large H icon crowds the 'Huzzah' wordmark, the '-Helen Keller' attribution floats far from its quote, and the woman photo is lost, leaving only washed-out sky. B keeps the logo, 'Huzzah' and 'Since 1982' together and sets the info text on one baseline, but '-Helen Keller' is crammed against 'or' as tiny two-line text, the left and right ends are empty while the middle is crowded, and the key image is also lost.

A: logo jammed against top-left edge with 'Huzzah' tucked underneath and touching it, the tagline and the merged 'address huzzah.dk' line sit on one ragged baseline row, and the hero woman is cropped out, leaving bland sky. The dividers are lost and 'Helen Keller' is split into a tiny two-line orphan. B: the logo is visibly stretched vertically and runs almost edge to edge, and the 'Huzzah'/'Since 1982' text overlaps it (a brand collision). It also loses the hero image and splits the attribution into tiny text, though the tagline and address are grouped better.

Both reflow the quote into a narrow column with bad wrapping: 'to' sits alone on its own line, 'men.' and 'have done it well.' keep the original hard breaks, and the attribution is indented off the text's left edge with dead space below it. A also shrinks the ram skull to a tiny thumbnail and pushes it left, and the yellow bar no longer crosses the skull the way it does in the original. B keeps the skull larger and closer to the original's yellow-bar overlay, so it stays more faithful, but it has the same typesetting problems.

A is a reasonable left-to-right banner: headline, then a stacked info column (gallery, URL, dates), then the artwork. But the info text is tiny at this size, the artwork is shrunk to a small thumbnail, so the poster's main visual feels trivial, and the original's rules and white frame are gone. B is clearly broken: the URL is dropped, a stray pipe is left on 'NOVAK GALLERY|', and the dates wrap awkwardly as 'JUNE 5 TO / JULY 3'. An empty white box floats meaninglessly in the middle, and the artwork is jammed against and cut off by the right edge.

A: one of the horizontal rules runs straight across the dot artwork, which is a collision. The headline is undersized for the canvas, the white frame is gone, and stray divider fragments (a tick on the right, two vertical lines at the bottom) float around. The details are split into three widely spaced lines, which leaves the right column scattered and empty. B: the big headline and grouped details make a clear left-to-right banner, and the framed artwork is kept. It still has flaws: the two top rules float off by themselves away from the headline, stray tick marks sit above the headline and on the frame's top edge, and the inner white frame has shrunk to an arbitrary off-centre box.

A stays faithful to the original, with a centered two-line headline, chevrons and nurse in the same order. Its main flaw is that the nurse's body is cut off flat about 50px above the bottom edge, leaving a purple strip under it instead of bleeding off the canvas as in the original. The headline is also a little tight to the top. B breaks the headline into four lines with orphan-like breaks ('10,000' / 'patients'), set left of centre with a dead area to its right. It blows the chevrons up into an oversized bottom-left graphic that competes with the headline and points at nothing, and shrinks the nurse into the corner with the same floating flat-cropped body, so the balance and hierarchy are off.

A: the chevron is blown up until it competes with the 4-line headline for attention. The nurse is shrunk to a small vignette floating above an empty strip at the bottom, so the hero image becomes trivial. B: keeps the chevron and nurse in proportion and at a sensible size, but the headline breaks onto 5 lines with an orphaned 'us', and 'patients' runs almost to the side edges. The whole group is also centred vertically, which leaves dead bands at the top and bottom, and the illustration no longer bleeds off the bottom edge as it did in the original.

Both break up the original's design: the two white bars sit in the far top and bottom corners instead of crossing the dark panel, and a small panel floats mid-canvas with a lot of dead image above and below it. A's headline is undersized for a 432×768 story but is still the larger and more readable of the two, and its wider panel has more even padding. B's headline is even smaller and is crammed into the panel with almost no vertical breathing room, which makes the main message weaker still.

A keeps a clear top-to-bottom order: kicker, then the teal ENERGY USE headline, then a decent-sized illustration. But the « » arrows have drifted far from 'YOUR EFFICIENT' and now float on their own. The illustration is cut off at the bottom edge, and the light-blue panel pieces poke out awkwardly at the left and right. B blows the arrow ornaments up into big, blurry, pixelated shapes and squeezes the illustration into a tiny thumbnail, so the key imagery is lost. It also leaves a stray blue strip on the left edge and a large empty area along the bottom.

A: the left kicker arrow is upscaled into a huge, blurry, pixelated blob, and the light-blue strip is cut off arbitrarily on the left edge. The kicker sits far from ENERGY USE with dead white space between them, so the headline group falls apart. B keeps a clear kicker→headline→illustration reading order with strong headline hierarchy. However, its kicker arrows have come loose and float above the text at the far edges. The illustration has lost its blue panel, the top of the canvas is empty, and two random light-blue blocks sit at the bottom like leftover fragments.

Both drop the woman holding the resume (only a stray hand fragment survives in the bottom-right corner), so the key image is gone. A keeps a clean left edge for the text, but its centred rules don't line up with the left-aligned copy, a bullet dot collides with the 's' of 'since 1980', the other dot floats on its own, and the vertical gaps are big and uneven. B is worse: the tilde is pushed off to the right, the four rules have different widths and centres, the dots float above 'since 1980' with no clear relationship to it, 'since 1980' is indented on its own axis, and the bottom 40% of the canvas is dead space.

Both crop out the woman and the resume, which is the original's key image, and leave only a stray hand fragment in the bottom-right corner, so fidelity is badly broken. In A the text is left-aligned but the rules are centred at different offsets, the swirl floats off to the right, and the diamonds sit apart from an unaligned 'since 1980', so the layout has no common axis. B is more consistent, with the text, long rules and swirl sharing a left edge, but one diamond collides with the 's' of 'since', the other drifts alone, and a large dead gap sits above the footer line.

A works as a two-column layout, with the photo panel on the left and the details on the right. Its flaws: the 'premiere' kicker is missing, the date is tiny and stranded mid-image, the right column floats in a large empty white area, and the dresscode line is as large as the headline.
